articles.title: China private factory PMI at 52.0 beats forecasts, output growth fastest since April
articles.desc: The beat offers some relief after Saturday’s weak official survey and may give modest support to China-sensitive assets such as the yuan, the Australian dollar and industrial metals at the start of the week. The price detail is less encouraging. Falling output and export charges driven by fierce com
articles.content: The beat offers some relief after Saturday’s weak official survey and may give modest support to China-sensitive assets such as the yuan, the Australian dollar and industrial metals at the start of the week. The price detail is less encouraging. Falling output and export charges driven by fierce competition point to continued disinflationary pressure from Chinese factories, which global markets could feel through cheaper goods exports. The gap between the export-tilted private survey and the broader official index also complicates Beijing’s stimulus calculations: it suggests pockets of strength in investment goods and exports even as wider activity softens. Confidence at a nine-month low is a reminder that the solid headline may not last if margins keep being squeezed. --- China’s export-focused manufacturers had a better October than the official data suggested, producing more and selling more, but only by cutting prices to win business in an increasingly crowded market. Summary: The RatingDog China General Manufacturing PMI, compiled by S&P Global, was 52.0 in October against 52.1 in September, above the 51.6 consensus It was the 11th straight month above 50, the longest run of improvement since mid-2021 Output grew at the fastest rate since April, led by investment goods, and new orders rose solidly for a 17th month, though export order growth slowed to a three-month low Output prices fell for the second time in three months and export charges dropped for the first time in nearly a year, as firms cited intense competition Input cost inflation eased, purchasing rose at the fastest pace since February, and supplier delivery times shortened Business confidence fell to a nine-month low on worries about input costs and competition China’s private-sector manufacturing gauge held firmly in expansion in October, offering a brighter view of the country’s factories than official data released at the weekend, though firms had to cut prices to keep orders flowing. The RatingDog China General Manufacturing PMI, compiled by S&P Global, was 52.0, little changed from 52.1 in September and above the 51.6 median forecast in a Reuters poll. It was the 11th straight month above the 50 mark that separates expansion from contraction, the longest such run since mid-2021. The data were released at 0145 GMT on Monday (2045 US Eastern on Sunday). The result contrasts with Saturday’s official manufacturing PMI from the National Bureau of Statistics, which slipped into contraction at 49.3. The RatingDog survey covers around 650 manufacturers and leans more toward export-oriented firms than the official poll, which samples more than 3,000 companies. Output grew at the fastest pace in six months, with growth spread across consumer, intermediate and investment goods, and strongest among investment goods makers. Total new orders rose for a 17th consecutive month at a solid pace, helped by new product launches, improved production capabilities and firms’ own sales efforts. New export orders increased for a fourth month, with firms citing more work from clients in Asia, Europe and Africa, but growth eased to a three-month low. Prices were the weak spot. Output charges fell for the second time in three months as intense competition pushed firms to discount, and export prices declined for the first time in nearly a year. Input costs kept rising, driven by metals and fuel, but at a slower pace than in September and below the year-to-date average. Firms stepped up purchasing at the fastest rate since February and built up input stocks at the strongest pace in five months. Supplier delivery times shortened for the first time in eight months. Hiring rose only marginally, leaving backlogs of work to keep building at a steady pace. Despite the solid activity, business confidence fell to a nine-month low, with some firms worried about elevated input prices and rising competition. RatingDog said cost pressures, price competition and subdued confidence warranted attention, though it expects the manufacturing PMI to remain in expansion in the near term. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

Legal challenges have kept the project in a 14-year stalemate since its initial application for a state permit. “We stand by our commitments to work together to see that the local communities and State, and our shareholders, benefit from this project as we continue to uphold our commitment to always operate with best practices to protect the people, land, air, and water,” said the executive chair of Texas-based enCore Energy, William Sheriff, in a June after the company received federal permits. articles.desc: The benchmark DSEX index dropped 32.29 points, or 0.60%, to settle at 5,385.15 points, down from 5,417.44 points in the previous session.
articles.content: Corporate earnings gloom drags DSEX down for second straight session | The Business Standard Corporate earnings gloom drags DSEX down for second straight session Last modified: 01 November, 2026, 10:01 pm Confidence Cement exits battery business with Tk11.34cr stake sale BAT Bangladesh's Q3 profit plunges 67%, shares fall 4.95% Mir Akhter Hossain shares plunge 12% on zero dividend declaration Titas Gas narrows FY26 loss to Tk595cr, recommends 2% cash dividend DBL's Parkway Packaging eyes Tk78cr IPO with Tk30 premium The benchmark DSEX index dropped 32.29 points, or 0.60%, to settle at 5,385.15 points, down from 5,417.44 points in the previous session. Last modified: 01 November, 2026, 10:01 pm Dhaka Stock Exchange. File Photo: Collected The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) extended its losing streak for a second consecutive session today (1 November), as disappointing corporate earnings and dividend declarations, coupled with persistent economic challenges, continued to dampen investor sentiment. The benchmark DSEX index dropped 32.29 points, or 0.60%, to settle at 5,385.15 points, down from 5,417.44 points in the previous session. The blue-chip DS30 index fell 0.88% to 2,068.43 points, while the Shariah-based DSES index declined 0.45% to 1,045.93 points. Keep updated, follow The Business Standard's Google news channel Market turnover also declined, falling 14.6% to Tk482.19 crore from Tk564 crore in the previous session, indicating a slowdown in trading activity. Textile stocks dominated turnover, accounting for 20.5% of the total, followed by General Insurance at 17.3% and Bank stocks at 11.3%, according to EBL Securities. Of the 387 issues traded on the DSE, 190 declined, 151 advanced and 46 remained unchanged, reflecting a predominantly negative market trend. According to EBL Securities' daily market commentary, investor concerns over the market's near-term outlook intensified amid ongoing corporate earnings disclosures and persistent domestic economic headwinds. Despite intermittent recovery attempts, selling pressure dominated the session as risk-averse investors continued to reduce their equity exposure. Disappointing earnings and dividend announcements by several large-cap companies further weakened market sentiment. All major large-cap sectors posted negative returns during the session, according to BRAC EPL Stock Brokerage's market commentary. Food and Allied led the losers, declining 2.69%, followed by Bank stocks at 1.27%, Non-Bank Financial Institutions at 1.06%, Engineering at 0.90%, Telecommunications at 0.64%, Pharmaceuticals at 0.26% and Fuel and Power at 0.25%. EBL Securities' sector-wise analysis also showed broad-based weakness, with Jute recording the steepest decline of 5.5%, followed by Food at 2.7% and Travel at 1.7%. However, some sectors bucked the downward trend. Mutual Funds gained 2.9%, General Insurance rose 1.1% and Textiles advanced 0.8%. Block trades accounted for 4.7% of total market turnover yesterday, according to BRAC EPL Stock Brokerage. Matin Spinning Mills emerged as the most traded stock, with shares worth Tk17.5 crore changing hands. Its share price gained 9.8% during the session. Meanwhile, the Chittagong Stock Exchange (CSE) also closed lower. Its Selective Categories' Index (CSCX) fell 45.9 points, while the All Share Price Index (CASPI) declined 82 points. Conservative Polish MP-turned-MEP Dominik Tarczyński shared an infographic summarizing his viral video exposing the modus operandi of the larger coup that liberal Prime Minister Donald Tusk is attempting, which goes beyond his government's armed takeover of the Constitutional Tribunal. According to Tarczyński, Tusk plans to oust conservative President Karol Nawrocki if successful, after which he'll take over the Central Bank, introduce the euro, and transfer Poland's gold to Germany. About his last three points, Poland's national currency remains strong, and its central bank has said it will raise its gold reserves to 700 tonnes, which would make them the 10th largest in the world. As of early this year, the Polish Central Bank has more gold than the European Central Bank, which is based in Frankfurt. Conservative grey cardinal Jarosław Kaczyński once accused Tusk of being a "German agent" due to how suspiciously close he's been to Germany throughout his career. Tarczyński's warning about Tusk's plans should therefore be taken seriously. Former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki, who now leads the Rozwój Plus (R+, Development Plus) party that broke from Kaczyński's "Law & Justice" (PiS per its Polish abbreviation) earlier this year, warned of civil war if Tusk isn't stopped and accused him of wanting to cancel next fall's Sejm elections. Reputable polling indicates that the ruling liberal coalition will lose and be replaced by a coalition between the aforementioned two conservative parties and the two libertarian-nationalist ones. Sławomir Mentzen, who's the co-leader of the Confederation Liberty and Independence (simply Confederation) libertarian-nationalist opposition party, also warned about civil war but suggested a detailed plan for resetting the Constitutional Tribunal as a means of averting it. This could pair with Morawiecki's proposal for an immediate vote of no confidence against Tusk and the formation of a technical government led by Marek Jurek till early elections are held in order to de-escalate the crisis. As a reminder, Nawrocki officially described the actions of Tusk's government as violating the constitutional order through the takeover of a constitutional state body by force, and Head of his International Policy Office Marcin Przydacz explained to the world why this is illegal. It's accordingly perceived by the opposition as a judicial coup, one which the European Commission predictably supports but which a police trade union warned against continuing, so some members might defy Tusk. If the larger coup that Tusk is attempting is successful through his attempted takeover of the Constitutional Tribunal, ousting of Nawrocki, subsequent takeover of the Central Bank, introduction of the euro, and transfer of Poland's gold to Germany, then Poland will be subordinated to Germany. That goal was identified here as his main motive in order to derail Nawrocki's EU reform plans and Poland's rise as a regional power for facilitating the EU's transformation into a German-dominated federation. "Poland's Ruling Liberals Are Already Blaming Russia For Their Attempted Judicial Coup", and there are fears that "Tusk Permitted The Riot Police To Use Lethal Force To Put Down Anti-Coup Protests", so peacefully protesting Poles might be killed on the false pretext of being "Russian agents". If members of Tusk's coalition don't defect during the vote of no confidence, and the police later kill some anti-coup protesters, then Nawrocki might call in the military to stop Germany's takeover of Poland by proxy. articles.desc: Tirunelveli inaugurates a weekly organic farmers’ market to connect growers directly with consumers, boosting earnings and access to organic produce.
articles.content: Tirunelveli Collector inaugurates weekly organic farmers’ market - The Hindu Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Unlock these with Subscription Tirunelveli Collector inaugurates weekly organic farmers’ market - November 01, 2026 09:25 pm IST - TIRUNELVELI: The newly inaugurated organic vegetable weekly market at Maharaanagar in Tirunelveli . | Photo Credit: A. SHAIKMOHIDEEN Collector Anand Mohan on Sunday inaugurated a weekly organic farmers’ market at Palayamkottai in the district. Speaking at the event, he said there was growing interest among consumers in purchasing organically grown products. However, farmers engaged in organic farming and production of value-added products often struggled to fetch remunerative prices for their produce. Hence, the weekly market had been established to bring organic farmers and consumers together to provide a platform for sale of produce directly while also making organic products more accessible to the public, he added. Organic farmers and farmer producers organisations wishing to participate in the market must possess any of the natural farming certificates issued by the Department of Seed and Organic Certification. Nine stalls had been set up in the first phase, with arrangements made to benefit 25 farmers through the initiative, he added. In Tirunelveli district, the sale of organically grown vegetables, fruits and value added products had commenced at three three farmers markets located at Maharaja Nagar in Palayamkottai, Melapalayam and NGO Colony. Mr. Mohan said the aim of the initiative was to enable farmers engaged in organic farming to market their produce directly to the public without intermediaries, ensuring better return for them while providing consumers access to organically grown products. articles.content: Woman quits $75,000 Chicago job to live remotely in Yellowstone National Park for $96 monthly rent | United States Woman quits $75,000 Chicago job to live remotely in Yellowstone National Park for $96 monthly rent At 26, Zoe De La Paz made $75,000 on a Chicago job as a mechanical designer. However, a trip to Yellowstone National Park changed everything. La Paz lived remotely for a few months at the Mammoth Village in Yellowstone National Park, where she worked as a seamstress. “Living and working in a national park is honestly sometimes emotionally overwhelming for me just because it’s just so indescribably beautiful,” said the 26-year-old woman on her big life change. La Paz paid $96 a month in rent while living there, and she often shared social media posts documenting her life in Yellowstone National Park in Wyoming. One Chicago Hits 800 Episodes as Chicago Fire Nears 300th Broadcast “A day in my life as a seamstress in Yellowstone,” she captioned one Instagramseries said, “This is truly one of the most beautiful, unreal places in the world. Just like being here has changed my life. ” Sharing what made her decide to live there in the first place, La Paz said, “It was what made me realize that life was too short and that I was very unhappy at my corporate job. ”The seamstress, who gave viewers a glimpse of her life in Mammoth Village, shared videos of her day at work, her hikes, her explorations of nature and local spots, and what the local laundry shops were like, among other things. The 26-year-old woman also talked about why she switched careers and chose this life, saying, “I didn’t have any sort of emotional connection or tie to the work that I was doing, which made it so hard to be fulfilled by it. ”“It was almost reaching a point of burnout, it really was one of those moments for me where I felt, I need to act now,” she continued. Zoe De La Paz often shared glimpses of her life in Mammoth Village in Yellowstone National Park. By: @ZOETERNAL/INSTAGRAM She further explained that corporate life was not meant for her. “I realized that I wanted this life more than I wanted the comfortability that a corporate job gave me,” she said. Her love for sewing dates back to her teen days when she took it up as a hobby. “I started sewing when I was 14 years old. Growing up in a really small town with not much to do, I was just left to my own devices in my basement and with my grandmother’s old sewing machine. ”entry, La Paz summed up her time there, writing, “My season has had its fair share of growing pains and annoyances as one would expect, but I am so indescribably grateful for this time at Yellowstone. ” Get an alert when there is news on United States News MLB Option Decisions: Alcantara $75 Million Guaranteed as Mets Keep Bichette Deal MLB teams made major option decisions, with Miami exercising Alcantara's $21 million option and Boston declining Gray's $30 million option while several players hit free agency. articles.desc: India advances Project 18A: in-principle nod for next-gen stealth destroyers costing ~₹80,000 cr, boosting indigenous, multi-domain naval capabilities.
articles.content: India plans next-generation stealth destroyers to counter growing maritime threats - The Hindu Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Unlock these with Subscription India plans next-generation stealth destroyers to counter growing maritime threats Defence Acquisition Council gives in-principle nod to futuristic warships at likely cost of ₹80,000 cr; will be equipped with advanced sensors, weapons; delivery to begin five to 10 years after contract is signed - November 01, 2026 09:21 pm IST - NEW DELHI The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has recently accorded in-principle approval to the futuristic warships under Project 18A. | Photo Credit: Sandeep Saxena The government has given a major push to the Indian Navy’s next-generation destroyer programme amid the growing maritime security , both of which are strengthening their own underwater warfare capabilities. The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has recently accorded in-principle approval to the futuristic warships under Project 18A. The delivery of the warships is expected to begin five to 10 years after the contract is signed, given the complexity and scale of the programme. A senior Defence Ministry official confirmed the development. The proposed programme, estimated to cost around ₹80,000 crore, aims to develop a new generation of stealth-guided missile destroyers equipped with advanced weapons, sensors, and technologies, the official said. The warships are expected to have nearly 75% indigenous content, with both defence public sector undertakings (DPSUs) and private sector companies eligible to participate in the competitive bidding process, the official added. Bolstering deterrence through submarine dominance The programme assumes significance as China continues to expand its naval presence in the Indian Ocean Region and enhance its submarine fleet, while Pakistan is also strengthening its underwater warfare capabilities with the induction of advanced submarines. A China-led trilateral nexus as India’s new challenge The evolving security environment has underscored the need for India to strengthen its surface combat fleet and maintain a credible maritime deterrence across the Indian Ocean region. Several existing destroyers of the Indian Navy are due for decommissioning in coming years, making the induction of advanced frontline surface combatants essential to maintaining the fleet’s operational strength, the official added. Water ingress onboard INS Kesari reported at Vizag Naval Dockyard; no casualties The futuristic destroyers, to be designed by the Navy’s Warship Design Bureau, are expected to feature significantly more advanced systems than the Visakhapatnam-class destroyers. These warships are likely to have enhanced firepower, sophisticated surveillance sensors, improved air defence systems, and advanced anti-submarine warfare capabilities, providing the Navy with greater operational flexibility against emerging maritime threats. The Indian Navy currently operates around 12 or 13 relatively new guided-missile destroyers, which form the backbone of its surface combat fleet and provide capabilities across air defence, anti-surface warfare, and anti-submarine operations. These include the Visakhapatnam-class, Kolkata-class, and Delhi-class destroyers. The existing warships are equipped with an array of advanced weapon systems, including BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles, surface-to-air missiles, naval guns, close-in weapon systems, and anti-submarine warfare equipment. The next-generation destroyers are expected to substantially enhance India’s firepower, surveillance, and multi-domain combat capabilities. articles.title: Short-range air defense systems with 360-degree turret installed at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate
articles.desc: Avenger features a 360-degree rotating turret with two missile pods mounted on a Humvee's heavy chassis and can fire FIM-92 Stinger missiles.
articles.content: Short-range air defense systems installed at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate Avengers, a short-range air defense system, and Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) capabilities have been deployed to protect President Trump. The system's upgraded Stinger missile provides on-the-go defense against aerial threats, including drones. Pulsar-based electronic warfare systems, part of the UAS, can use radio-frequency signals to detect and disrupt hostile drones. Amid the heightened concerns about President Donald J. Trump’s safety, the U.S. Secret Service has deployed AN/TWQ-1 Avenger short-range air defense systems (SHORADS) near his residence at the Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, Florida. These systems, manufactured by Boeing, are mounted atop the U.S. Army’s 4X4 military trucks, the Heavy High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle (HMMWV), or Humvees, and were also installed about three miles west of Donald J. Trump International Airport. The Avenger features a 360-degree rotating turret with two missile pods mounted on a Humvee’s heavy chassis and can fire FIM-92 . Each launcher has a capacity to hold four of these heat-seeking surface-to-air missiles and operates day and night in all weather conditions. A gunner guards the Avenger from the firing station between the two missile pods and operates the launcher. The crew can also operate the weapon system from a remote control unit up to meters away from the firing line. As operational requirements change, the highly mobile Avenger systems can be repositioned to defend against incoming aerial threats, offering air defense for the maneuver force. The upgraded missile system provides on-the-go defensive protection for troops on the ground and in homeland security operations, countering aerial threats, including US Army’s HADES spy plane completes first flight, marks major leap in deep-sensing capabilities This Chinese warship could operate without a crew, launch missile salvos Harop-like loitering munition offers clues about North Korea’s future unmanned-aerial warfare Military airspace surveillance to get major boost, reveal aircraft’s accurate position with new radar Aging warships to get Western eyes to improve naval gun targeting with modern tech These infrared-guided weapons were originally designed to defeat helicopters, aircraft, cruise missiles, and larger unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). They engage aerial targets at low altitudes and are designed to protect specific locations rather than defend an entire region. According to photos shared on online platforms, two such Avengers have been deployed near the Trump International Airport. Besides the Avenger missile systems, North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) and North American Aerospace Defense Command have also deployed Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) capabilities to support the Secret Service, These counter-drone flyaway kits that are rapidly deployable help to spot, classify, and track UAVs. The systems also have the ability to react to drone threats that are detected using both passive and active sensor systems, such as electro-optical and infrared cameras, or Ku-band radars. Pulsar-based electronic warfare systems, part of the UAS, can use radio-frequency signals to detect and disrupt hostile drones. They rely on jamming the Global Positioning System (GPS) signals of hostile drones to neutralize or spoof them. However, if the jamming fails, the kits recruit kinetic interceptors or other defeat mechanisms. Earlier this week, soldiers in the United States tested rapidly deployable . They trained on Trust Automation’s Rapidly Deployable Small-Unmanned Air Defense System, or RD-SUADS, a palletized counter-drone system. RD-SUADS is the air-transportable member of Trust Automation’s Small-Unmanned Air Defense System family, designed to detect, track, identify, and defeat small drones at bases and deployed sites. The company built it to be shipped and set up quickly without relying on local power. Get the latest in

articles.title: University of Cambridge scientist died in Spain train crash
articles.desc: Tributes have been paid to Dr Marta Shahbazi, described as a ‘brilliant young researcher’
articles.content: University of Cambridge scientist died in Spain train crash | The Standard University of Cambridge scientist died in Spain train crash Tributes have been paid to Dr Marta Shahbazi, described as a ‘brilliant young researcher’ Tributes are paid to Dr Marta Shahbazi, described as a "brilliant young researcher" at the University of Cambridge, who was on her way to collect an award for scientific excellence researcher was killed in the deadly Spanish train crash that has killed at least 69 people. Dr Marta Shahbazi, a scientist at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in Cambridge, was on a train that collided with another near the town of Urda in central Spain on Wednesday. A mother to two young children had been travelling to collect a prize for scientific excellence. Dr Shahbazi carried out research into the early stages of human embryo development, according to the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) agency, which the LMB is a part of. Dr Shahbazi “wrote eloquently about balancing her family and career”, the UKRI said, “serving as a much-admired role model for a ‘mother scientist’, a term she used to describe herself”. She had been due to receive the scientific excellence prize from the Spanish Society of Developmental Biology at a conference which began on the day of the crash. The LMB has paid tribute to the “inspiring” scientist, who was a group leader in its Cell Biology Division and an affiliate associate professor at the University of Cambridge. Dr Shahbazi is listed on the university’s website as a principal investigator at its Stem Cell Institute. The laboratory said: “The LMB is deeply saddened by the tragic death of our colleague Marta Shahbazi, group leader in the Cell Biology Division. “Marta was on a train that collided with another near Urda, Spain, on Wednesday October 28, as she was travelling to receive the scientific excellence prize from the Spanish Society of Developmental Biology. “Marta was an inspiring, talented and passionate scientist. Her death is a profound shock and a huge loss. “Our thoughts are with her family, friends and colleagues at this extremely difficult time. “The LMB is offering support to members of its community as they navigate this tragic loss.” Director of the University of Cambridge Stem Cell Institute (CSCI), Prof Bertie Gottgens, said its community is “shocked and deeply saddened” by Dr Shahbazi’s death. Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean dies aged 34 Ciara Mageean put Ireland on the map again for middle distance running Match of the Day viewers issue new Chapman verdict after complaints Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style He added: “Marta led her primary research group at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) alongside her roles as an affiliate principal investigator and affiliate assistant professor at the CSCI. “Across both institutes, she was highly respected for her pioneering research on early human development and valued for her collaborative spirit. Her creativity, passion, and generosity will be greatly missed.” At least 69 people are thought to have lost their lives in the disaster, which was the country’s second high-speed rail crash this year. Both collisions occurred on the same line between the central city of , in the Andalucia region in the south of the country. Three days of national mourning were observed from Thursday, with Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez describing the incident as a “tragedy” and promising an investigation.

articles.title: Exploding stars carved a giant bubble in a neighboring galaxy
articles.desc: Hubble reveals a vast cosmic bubble where massive stars cleared away gas, only for the compressed material around it to begin forming thousands of new stars.
articles.content: Exploding stars carved a giant bubble in a neighboring galaxy Exploding stars carved a giant bubble in a neighboring galaxy Hubble reveals a vast cosmic bubble where massive stars cleared away gas, only for the compressed material around it to begin forming thousands of new stars. Today’s Image of the Day from the European Space Agency reveals an enormous stellar nursery where generations of stars have reshaped the surrounding landscape. Bright young stars, dark clouds of dust, and glowing gas fill the scene. Near the middle lies an enormous empty-looking cavity. Far from being quiet, this hollow region records some of the most violent events in the lives of massive stars. The nebula sits in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small neighboring galaxy about 160,000 light-years from Earth. The Large Magellanic Cloud is the largest of the small galaxies orbiting the Its relative closeness gives astronomers an unusually detailed view of places where stars are being born. N44 lies within the constellation Dorado and contains a mix of young stars, thick gas, and dust. Its most striking feature is a vast central cavity measuring roughly 210 by 140 light-years. Astronomers call this kind of structure a superbubble. The stars inside the cavity helped create it. Massive young stars throw material into space through powerful stellar winds. Some eventually explode as supernovae, releasing enormous amounts of energy and pushing surrounding gas outward. Over time, those forces cleared much of the material from the central region of N44. Instead of simply disappearing, the displaced gas accumulated around the edges. It formed the dense, dusty shell visible around the superbubble today. The shell also contains young stars, suggesting that material compressed along the bubble’s edges may be helping new generations form. Gas compressed along the bubble’s boundary can become dense enough to collapse under its own gravity, forming new stars. N44 therefore gives astronomers a chance to study several stages of star formation within the same complex. Researchers want to measure how long the process takes, beginning when cold clouds of gas collapse into dense knots and ending when nuclear fusion starts inside a Researchers used Hubble to conduct a remarkably large census of N44. The telescope catalogued nearly half a million stars, including stars belonging to the complex and unrelated objects lying along the same line of sight. Nearly 30,000 of the objects are pre-main-sequence stars. These are young stars that have not yet reached the long, relatively stable stage of life in which hydrogen fusion powers their cores. Finding so many of them gives researchers a large population for studying the earliest phases of stellar development. Young, low-mass stars can be difficult to detect, especially when they sit among brighter objects and glowing clouds of gas. Hubble’s sensitivity and sharp spatial resolution allow astronomers to separate many of these faint points of light even in densely packed stellar neighborhoods. The observations also help scientists investigate the masses of newborn stars. That matters because the amount of mass a star acquires during largely determines what happens during the rest of its life, from how brightly it shines to how long it survives. Ultraviolet radiation pouring from massive stars energizes the gas surrounding N44’s superbubble. That radiation helps produce the nebula’s bright glow and reveals smaller structures scattered throughout the larger complex. Astronomer Karl Henize catalogued these individual features during the 1950s. One of them, N44F, appears near the upper-right portion of the Hubble view. Unlike the enormous central superbubble, N44F was shaped largely by the fierce wind of a single hot, massive star. Radiation and stellar winds from that star have pushed against nearby material, producing a smaller interstellar bubble. observations have also revealed pillars of dusty gas shaped by the intense activity. articles.title: Hubble Is Slowly Falling Toward Earth, and NASA Has a Bold Plan to Save It
articles.desc: NASA is exploring a commercial rescue strategy to raise Hubble's orbit and extend the legendary space telescope's scientific life.
articles.content: Hubble Is Slowly Falling Toward Earth, and NASA Has a Bold Plan to Save It alive: asking commercial space companies to help raise its orbit before atmospheric drag brings the legendary observatory back toward Earth. After more than 35 years in space, Hubble could receive an unexpected lifeline from a new generation of satellite-servicing technology. NASA Turns to Private Companies to Extend Hubble’s Life has transformed humanity’s understanding of the universe, capturing distant galaxies, studying planetary atmospheres, and revealing cosmic structures previously hidden from astronomers. Now, the observatory faces a challenge that scientific instruments alone cannot overcome: its gradually declining orbit. , the agency is exploring opportunities for commercial companies to provide orbital servicing that could extend Hubble’s operational lifetime. The goal is to identify technologies capable of safely boosting the telescope into a higher orbit, reducing the atmospheric drag that is slowly pulling it toward Earth. has emphasized the scientific and economic arguments for preserving the observatory rather than allowing its mission to end prematurely. “Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset already on orbit, we owe it to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to explore them. Extending Hubble’s life would mean more discoveries, more science, and more opportunities to expand our understanding of the universe.” The initiative reflects a broader change in space operations. Capabilities once associated primarily with government missions are increasingly being developed by commercial providers, potentially creating new options for maintaining valuable spacecraft already in orbit. NASA issued a Request for Information to learn more about industry capabilities for in-space servicing to support the agency’s Hubble Space Telescope: https://t.co/qqNozR5Xq6 https://t.co/1IyK0wl1Z0 Why Hubble’s Declining Orbit Is Becoming a Growing Concern , Hubble was designed to be serviced by astronauts. Five shuttle servicing missions subsequently repaired, upgraded, and maintained the observatory, allowing it to operate far beyond its initial expectations. The final servicing mission took place in 2009. Since the retirement of the Space Shuttle program in 2011, NASA has lacked the same established capability to send astronauts to Hubble for maintenance. Meanwhile, Hubble continues to orbit Earth in the upper reaches of the atmosphere, where thin traces of gas create drag. Although the force is weak, its cumulative effect gradually reduces the telescope’s altitude. Solar activity complicates the situation. When the Sun becomes more active, it heats Earth’s upper atmosphere, causing it to expand. This increases atmospheric density at satellite altitudes and can accelerate orbital decay. Without an intervention, Hubble will eventually descend far enough for atmospheric reentry. The precise timing depends on atmospheric conditions, solar activity, and the telescope’s evolving orbit. could delay that outcome and preserve the opportunity to continue scientific observations. Raising Hubble’s altitude would not repair aging instruments or eliminate hardware failures, but it could address one of the external threats to the observatory’s future. A New Generation of Space Technology Could Give Hubble More Years The growing commercial satellite-servicing industry offers NASA an alternative to traditional astronaut-led maintenance missions. Companies are developing spacecraft designed to approach, inspect, capture, reposition, and potentially service other objects in orbit. articles.content: Cuban Charada Printable PDF: Decoding the 100 Numbers and Their Meanings Cuban Charada Printable PDF: Decoding the 100 Numbers and Their Meanings The Cuban charada links numbers from 1 to 100 with animals, objects, people, and situations. CiberCuba has assembled a downloadable and printable PDF of this charada, enabling users to explore these popular associations without the hassle of looking up each number individually. This document draws from the list of 100 numbers in the Cuban charada as previously published by the outlet. It includes both the primary symbols and additional equivalences found in that compilation. The file lists numbers from 1 to 100, sorted in ascending order, along with their corresponding meanings. Each number can have multiple associations: for instance, number 1 is linked to a horse, sun, inkwell, camel, and small fish. This guide features five pages with selectable text, allowing users to utilize PDF reader search functions to quickly find specific words, in addition to browsing directly through the number column. Searching for Numbers Linked to Dreams or Symbols To search for a specific number, open the document and use the search function of your PDF reader. On most computers, this is accessible with Ctrl + F, or Command + F on a Mac. For mobile devices, locate the magnifying glass icon or the search option within the document. Enter a specific word, such as horse, butterfly, or money, and examine the results. Some words appear in multiple entries, so it's important to read the full context rather than stopping at the first match. For example, the butterfly is associated with number 2, whereas the large butterfly is linked to 94. The dog appears at 15, while large dog, small dog, and medium dog appear at 12, 28, and 71, respectively. : The horse is listed at number 1, and the cat at 4. The list further specifies tiger cat at 14, yellow cat at 18, and fine cat at 20. : Money is associated with numbers 10 and 38. Water is found at 89, alongside other equivalents. : The phone corresponds to number 70, and mother to 82, each with additional symbols that can be found using the same search method. : Doctor appears at both 26 and 80; rain is noted at 11 and 99. These repetitions are part of the associations used to compile the document. The charada is not a dictionary with a single answer per word. Instead, it provides various associations for each number, with some repeating or modifying based on characteristics like the size of an animal. The PDF retains CiberCuba's published version and should be viewed as a cultural reference, rather than a scientific interpretation of dreams or a predictor of outcomes. Consulting a symbol does not make its number more likely to win in a lottery. You can open and download the Cuban charada PDF by using the save function in your PDF viewer. To access it offline, ensure the PDF is saved on your device and not just open in a browser tab. The document is designed in letter size. Before printing, select your paper size and check the print preview. If using A4, the fit-to-page option will adjust the content for the sheet. Print all five pages or just the ones you need. The numbers and meanings are in text format, allowing for reference even in a black-and-white printout. The Cuban charada is a traditional system that assigns specific meanings, such as animals, objects, or situations, to numbers from 1 to 100. You can download the PDF to search for meanings associated with numbers. Use the search function in your PDF reader to locate specific words or numbers. No, the charada is a cultural reference and not a tool for predicting lottery outcomes. Numbers aligned with symbols do not increase winning chances.
